purpose: This unit covers the tested Solidity core of the HKMN 'process' pipeline: a single-cycle vault (PegCycleVault) that an off-chain trusted 'authorizer' funds from a ProcessBudget skim, drives through an arbitrary outbound route (the real-world pack purchase would happen off-chain, invisibly to the contract), and later authorizes a return payout that is committed via a 1024-leaf canonical merkle-sum manifest (CanonicalMerkleSum/PayoutCommitment) and paid out permissionlessly to individual HKMN holders (HolderSettlement). Around this sits shared 2-step role handover/fee-liability plumbing (MoneyRoles + FeeAccounting, exercised via MoneyRoles.t.sol), an off-chain-issuance verification guard for the HKMN token itself (HookemonIssuance), and Robinhood-chain Uniswap v4 binding/fee-quadrant math (RobinhoodBindings, RobinhoodV4PoolManager, plus a 'blind' market-fees spec-and-adapter suite). A large fraction of the 'blind/*' subtree is design-freeze documentation encoded as either dead abstract Solidity contracts or plain JSON files checked for shape only by Node tests -- it does not exercise the real token or a real liability/claim/custody path end to end.

MoneyRoles: RoleState{programmableBeneficiary,treasury,operations}, PendingRoleTransfer{role,currentAccount,proposedAccount}, CycleBoundOperations{cycleId,operations}; proposeTreasury/acceptTreasury, proposeOperations/acceptOperations (2-step, no self/zero/cross-role), readRoles(cycleId); internal _authorizeProgrammableClaim/_authorizeTreasuryClaim/_bindCycleOperations/_authorizePayoutFunding/_authorizeHolderPayment/_currentTreasury; events RoleProposed/RoleAccepted(bytes32 role,address previous,address current)
ImmutableLaunchBinding: constructor(Binding) freezes bindingDigest immutably, no initialize()/reinitialize path

invariants: PegCycleVault: exactly one pending FundingAuthorization at a time; every identity field (chainId, hook, vault, usdg, operationsTrigger, bindingManifestDigest, outboundActionDigest, returnActionDigest, returnDestination, amount>0, expiresAt in future, requirementsRevision==56) must match exactly or the whole authorization is rejected atomically; nonce and cycleId are both globally one-shot (replay-proof) even across a rejected/expired authorization; executeOutbound requires the vault's USDG allowance to the route executor be fully consumed (RetainedAllowance revert otherwise) and moves the EXACT authorized amount; authorizePayout requires vault balance == rootSum exactly (>= minimumReturnUsdg, itself frozen at funding time) or it reverts without mutating state; FAILED is terminal/absorbing and only reachable with zero vault balance.

ProcessBudget/PayoutCommitment/HolderSettlement/MoneyRoles: all money-moving internal functions are behind a moneyPath modifier only the composing hook contract itself can enter (InternalEscalationProbe test proves an external contract cannot call the internal escalation surface even via delegated call patterns); programmableBeneficiary is fixed forever from construction (self-claim, self-destination only); treasury/operations liabilities and per-cycle bindings are frozen AT THE MOMENT of accrual/release, so a later 2-step handover never rewrites a historical epoch's beneficiary or a historical cycle's payer/operationsTrigger.

Fee split invariant (pervasive): total = executedUsdg*300/10000 (3.00% inclusive), programmable = executedUsdg*10/10000 (0.10%), treasury = executedUsdg*40/10000 (0.40%), process = total-programmable-treasury (2.50% target, floor remainder) -- programmable+treasury+process always exactly equals total (no dust), matching the repository-authoritative 0.10/0.40/2.50 split.

CanonicalMerkleSum: fixed depth 10 / 1024 leaves; leaf/node hashes are domain-separated by a versioned tag string plus (chainId,hook,cycleId,payoutId,manifestDigest[,index]); manifest entries must be strictly-ascending unique index, nonzero recipient, recipient != hook; internal-node sum addition reverts on uint256 overflow (checked add, not wrapping).

PayoutCommitment/HolderSettlement conservation: funded == paid + unpaid always, per payoutId, independent of any other payoutId or of direct/rogue USDG transfers into the hook (those create no recognized liability); a payoutId and its returnReceiptDigest are both permanently one-shot and cannot replay across cycles.

HolderSettlement: no manual recipient replacement, no batch pay, no worker/emergency-mode gate, no retry-with-different-recipient, no recover-entitlement path exists (verified by forbidden-selector probing) -- the merkle-sum leaf's recipient is the only ever-valid destination for that (payoutId,index).

RobinhoodBindings.ImmutableLaunchBinding: every one of 12 required identities, the PoolKey construction (currency ordering, tickSpacing!=0, poolLpFee==0, matching poolId), the 14-bit hookPermissionMask (every single bit must match exactly), hookSalt/hookInitCodeHash/hookDeployer (CREATE2 address must match), 3 provenance digests (source/abi/runtime sets), chainId==4663, requirementsRevision==54, architectureRevision==3, and the exact 300/10/40/9000bps constants must all match or construction reverts and no ETH balance moves; the contract exposes no initialize()/reinitialize path after construction.
stateTransitions: PegCycleVault.Lifecycle: EMPTY -[authorizeFunding + hook.fund exact amount]-> FUNDED -[executeOutbound by frozen operationsTrigger, exact route digest+target+selector+amount, allowance fully consumed]-> OUTBOUND -[authorizePayout, vault balance == rootSum exactly]-> RETURNED -[hook.consumePayoutAuthorization, transfers exact rootSum to hook]-> PAYOUT_COMMITTED -[a fresh authorizeFunding for a new cycleId succeeds, implicitly re-arming pending-authorization state]-> (next cycle's FUNDED path). At ANY point authorizer may call recordTerminalFailure (only once vault balance is 0) to move to the terminal, absorbing FAILED state; no transition out of FAILED exists in these tests.

MoneyRoles treasury/operations: current -[propose by current holder]-> pending(current,proposed) -[accept by proposed]-> proposed becomes current, pending cleared; a second propose replaces the still-open pending proposal; self/zero/cross-role/third-party calls are all rejected without mutating pending state.

HookemonIssuance.GuardStatus: UNPREPARED -[prepareOfficialIssuance by authority, one-shot]-> PREPARED_PROVIDER_CALL_UNAVAILABLE -[verifyIssuance by authority, one-shot, plan+observation+trace must match exactly]-> OBSERVATION_VERIFIED_PROVIDER_BINDING_PENDING (terminal in this file's tests; the actual on-chain provider binding step is out of scope here).
PermanentPositionCustody: unset -[finalizePosition(), requires custody already holds the NFT/liquidity position]-> positionReceived==true (terminal; finalizing twice reverts; no path back or onward).

testStatus: 15 concrete Solidity test contracts across process/, payout/, settlement/, access/, launch/, bindings/ and blind/market-fees/ are real Forge tests exercising real src/ contracts (not run here per instructions -- forge build/test was off-limits -- but every assertion path was traced by hand). Two large Solidity files are structurally DEAD: (1) test/blind/market-fees/BlindMarketFeesAcceptance.t.sol (820 lines, ~35 test_ functions) is `abstract contract BlindMarketFeesAcceptance` with NO concrete subclass anywhere in test/ or src/ (grep-confirmed) -- Forge only runs concrete contracts, so this file executes ZERO tests despite looking like a full P1-004 acceptance suite; its own `_deploy()` calls `BlindMarketFeesFixture.deploy()` which unconditionally reverts. (2) test/blind/token-roles/FixedSupplyBlindSpec.sol (565 lines, 17 test_ functions specifying the entire fixed-supply token contract) is likewise `abstract`; its only concrete subclass, FixedSupplyBindingTest, lives in FixedSupplyBinding.t.sol.disabled -- the `.disabled` extension means Foundry never compiles or runs it, and even its stub overrides all revert with BlindFixtureNotBound() by design. FixedSupplyPrepTest and BlindMarketFeesSchemaReadiness/Prep tests DO run, but only against synthetic fixture data / a standalone evidence library, never a real deployed HKMN token or full market-fees contract. BlindCanonicalMarketAdapter.t.sol is the one blind-suite exception: BlindCanonicalMarketConcreteAcceptance IS a real, non-abstract subclass and does exercise the real src/market/CanonicalMarket.sol callback logic. The 6 Node tests (3 files) under blind/payout-settlement/ were executed directly (`node --test`) during this review and all passed, but they only validate that 3 JSON specification files have the expected shape/constants ('interfaceBinding': 'deferred-until-frozen' in all three) -- they never touch a Solidity contract and describe requirements (P1-006/007/008, revision 55) that appear to already be implemented at revision 56 by ProcessBudget/PayoutCommitment/HolderSettlement, raising a revision-currency question (see openQuestions).
autonomyGaps: Nothing in this unit implements or tests a scheduler/interval, a Collector Crypt pack-buy/open/sell integration, a dashboard, or 'restart/kick a stuck cycle' beyond the single authorizer-only recordTerminalFailure call -- and that call only succeeds once the vault balance is already exactly zero. If an off-chain outbound action fails leaving a NONZERO but wrong-amount balance in the vault (state stuck at OUTBOUND), there is no tested path in this unit to either recover the funds or advance/reset the cycle: authorizePayout requires balance==rootSum exactly, and recordTerminalFailure requires balance==0. This is a concrete gap against the owner's 'restart/kick cycles that got stuck' dashboard requirement.

The entire 'automation' side of the owner's target -- buy pack, open pack, sell card, route USDG back, distribute pro rata -- happens OFF-CHAIN and is represented on-chain only as a single trusted 'authorizer' address calling authorizeFunding/authorizePayout with matching digests; there is no signature scheme, no multisig, no timelock, and no on-chain verification that the claimed outboundActionDigest/returnActionDigest correspond to any real Collector Crypt transaction. All of that trust is pushed to an off-chain service that does not exist in this unit's tested code (per repo facts, it lives in the unmerged codex/complete-v4-hook / codex/phase2-revision-57 branches).

No test in this unit exercises the real production Uniswap v4 hook that will actually be deployed via the Programmable launchpad; RobinhoodV4PoolManagerTest uses a hand-written 'PinnedInclusiveUsdgFeeHook' stand-in. Combined with the established fact that the Programmable Robinhood launchpad and canonical PoolKey are INTEGRATION_PENDING, there is currently no executable test anywhere in this unit of the actual hook that will collect the owner's 3% fee on Robinhood Chain.

There is no executable test anywhere in this unit of the real, deployed HKMN token contract's identity, fixed supply, 90/10 allocation, or transfer/ERC20 semantics -- the only candidate (FixedSupplyBlindSpec, 17 tests) is abstract and its sole binding is a disabled file. HookemonIssuance.t.sol tests a verification GUARD around an external mint event, not the token contract itself.

'Bei Bybit' / sale path: no code in this unit references Bybit, a CEX withdrawal, or any sale mechanism other than the abstract notion of an 'outbound route' + 'return' authorized digest pair; nothing here confirms or refutes the Collector Crypt-buyback hypothesis at the contract layer (that mapping would live in the off-chain automation service, not here).

_assertNoProjectPositionControl (and similarly RobinhoodV4PoolManager.t.sol's _assertNoPositionControl at line 412) proves an arbitrary third-party Caller contract cannot invoke the POSITION MANAGER's transferFrom/approve/decreaseLiquidity/collect for a token it doesn't own -- true of any ERC-721-owned position regardless of custody design. Neither test scans PermanentPositionCustody's OWN bytecode/selectors for a hidden withdraw/rescue path the way MoneyRoles.t.sol and HolderSettlement.t.sol do for their own contracts; the more rigorous per-selector custody probe (probePositionControl) exists only in the dead BlindMarketFeesAcceptance.t.sol. The 'no project control' claim for the 90% permanent launch position is therefore weaker in the executing test suite than the naming suggests.

The canonical manifest/leaf/node domain tags are hardcoded as 'HOOKEMON_PAYOUT_..._R55_A4_V1' (revision 55, architecture 4), while every FundingAuthorization/PayoutAuthorization fixture across PegCycleVault.t.sol, ProcessBudget.t.sol, PayoutCommitment.t.sol and HolderSettlement.t.sol uses requirementsRevision 56 and RobinhoodBindings.t.sol uses requirementsRevision 54 / architectureRevision 3. Three different revision/architecture numbers appear pinned into golden byte-level constants across this one unit's files; whether these are independently-versioned subsystems (by design) or drift between an updated policy and stale test fixtures is not determinable from these files alone.

requirementsRevision 55 with 'interfaceBinding': 'deferred-until-frozen', yet the scenario ids/expectations (process-release exact liability, payout-funding cycle-bound-operations, settlement permissionless-exact-recipient-credit, etc.) read as a near-exact behavioral description of the ALREADY-IMPLEMENTED-AND-TESTED ProcessBudget/PayoutCommitment/HolderSettlement contracts (revision 56 in their own test fixtures). If this JSON is meant to be the frozen spec those contracts implement, it is one requirements revision behind the code it should describe; if it describes a different (not-yet-built) minimal direct-release design, that should be stated explicitly rather than left implicit.

testAllEightQuadrantsUseZeroLpFeeAndOneInclusiveHookFee re-derives hookFee/specifiedDelta/amount0/amount1 by hand in the test itself (mirroring the production formula) rather than constructing them from an independent oracle; a bug shared between RobinhoodBindings.validateQuadrant and this test's mirrored math would not be caught.
